# FieldShore v4 Build Audit — 2026-06-14

This audit traced the v4 React/TypeScript app on `v4-redesign` for logic bugs, dead code, and over-engineering that `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` cannot see. **Confirmed: 19 broken findings (2 Critical, 8 High, 6 Medium, 3 Low — though one Low and one High are documented a11y/port exceptions), 12 dead-code findings, 4 over-engineering findings.** The single most important thing: the **inline one-step deploy path** (`AddShorePointModal.handleDeploy`) silently swallows per-point `StrutDeployed` commit failures — a partial deploy reports full success with a success haptic, leaving struts the operator believes are deployed sitting Pending; the same path also announces the wrong lane/status. A close second is the **soft-deleted grouped shore point that permanently dead-ends its surviving mate's advance**, and the **`Slider` committing on `pointercancel`** (a wet-screen ghost-commit of a lifecycle status). All three are reachable in the running app today. Note: the two over-capacity `pendingReason` findings are the *same bug* reported twice at different severities — deduped below to one High.

---

### Critical

**1 · Inline one-step deploy swallows commit failures — silent partial deploy** — `src/ui/operations/AddShorePointModal.tsx:291-306`
- **Claim:** In one-step (`inlineDeploy`) mode, `handleDeploy` loops `await commit({ type: 'StrutDeployed', … })` once per point but never inspects the returned `CommitResult`. `applyDeployTxn` throws → `{ok:false}` when stock hits zero (`inventoryStore.ts:50`). When stock runs out partway through the loop, the failed commits are discarded: those points stay Pending, no error surfaces, `commitHaptic()` fires as if success, `onAdded()` runs and the sheet closes. The two-step `AssignEquipmentSheet.handleDeploy` correctly checks `result.ok`/`result.reason` (lines 71-78); the inline path regressed that guard.
- **Evidence:** `for (const p of points) { await commit({ type:'StrutDeployed', … spId:p.id, deployedStrut:{model,source:item.apparatus,inventoryId} }); }` then unconditionally `commitHaptic(); onAdded?.(points); onClose();` — no result captured anywhere in the loop. The code comment even anticipates the missing toast ("deployed X of N").
- **Repro:** Start an op with one-step deploy on. Stock exactly 1 unit of a fitting strut. Add a shore point with Number of Shore Sets = 3 (3 struts). Find → Deploy: `applyDeployTxn` decrements 1→0, the 2nd and 3rd commits abort ("none available, L-8 abort"). Result: 1 point In Process, 2 silently left Pending, success haptic, no error, board announces "3 shore points added — Pending."
- **Fix:** Inspect each commit result; count successes; on any failure stop deploying further points, set `deployError`, and do not `commitHaptic()` for an all-fail case. Surface "Deployed X of N — the rest stayed Pending (out of stock)." Branch `onAdded` vs `onDeployed` on whether any deploy succeeded.

**2 · Soft-deleted grouped shore point permanently blocks its surviving mate's advance** — `src/ui/operations/OperationsBoard.tsx:442-451`
- **Claim:** `advanceDisabledReasonFor()` counts soft-deleted (`deletedAt != null`) members toward the group advance-gate. A soft-deleted point keeps `status:'pending'` (the reducer stamps `deletedAt` only — `reducer.test.ts:145`), so a deleted-while-Pending grouped member is counted forever in `stillPending`. The gate never clears and the surviving deployed mate can never slide In Process → Strut Set. The blocking point isn't rendered in any lane (`byStatus` filters `deletedAt` at line 490) — it only appears as a slim row in the Deleted section — so the crew sees "Waiting on group — 1 of 3 still Pending" with no Pending card to resolve.
- **Evidence:** `const mates = shorePoints.filter((s) => s.groupId === sp.groupId);` — **no** `s.deletedAt == null` filter, unlike `divisionsPresent`/`areasPresent`/`buildingsPresent`/`byStatus` which all guard it.
- **Repro:** Add a 3-Post (M1/M2/M3, shared groupId, all Pending). Delete M3 while Pending (soft-delete; M3 leaves the lanes). Deploy M1+M2 (→ process). Slide M1 to advance: `mates=[M1,M2,M3]`, `stillPending=[M3]=1` → "Waiting on group — 1 of 3 still Pending"; the advance Slider is `disabled`. M1/M2 stuck in In Process indefinitely. Only Restoring M3 un-sticks it, with no on-board signal that the phantom *is* the deleted point.
- **Fix:** `const mates = shorePoints.filter((s) => s.groupId === sp.groupId && s.deletedAt == null);` and recount off the filtered list — matching the `deletedAt == null` discipline already used everywhere else in this file.

### High

**3 · `pendingReasonFor` mislabels an over-capacity opening as `no-match`** — `src/core/shorepoint/pendingReason.ts:24-29` (schema: `src/core/schema/shorepoint.ts:56`)
> *Deduped:* this was reported twice (Medium "board-glance only" + High "safety-relevant"). It is one bug; the higher severity governs.
- **Claim:** When a Pending point fits geometrically but `estimatedLoad` exceeds 4-strut capacity, the engine returns ONLY an `exceedsCapacity` sentinel from both the stocked run and the catalog run. `stocked.some(c => !c.exceedsCapacity)` is false (sentinel only), so it falls to the catalog run, also sentinel-only, so `catalog.some(c => !c.exceedsCapacity)` is false → returns `'no-match'`. `OperationsBoard.tsx:458` stamps this onto the Pending card unconditionally; `ShorePointCard.tsx:16` renders "No matching strut — nothing fits this opening at this load." That is a geometry verdict; the truth is the geometry is fine and the load is too high (needs >4 struts / rescue-engineering consult). The `PendingReason` enum has no value to express load-too-high.
- **Evidence:** `if (stocked.some((c) => !c.exceedsCapacity)) return undefined; const catalog = findForShorePoint(sp, null); return catalog.some((c) => !c.exceedsCapacity) ? 'no-inventory' : 'no-match';` — verified live (132″ T-Shore, `estimatedLoad` 60000, LS 1016 in stock) prints `STOCKED:[{model:'LS 1016',exceeds:true}] CATALOG:[{model:'LS 406',exceeds:true}] REASON: no-match`. `schema/shorepoint.ts:56` — `PendingReason = z.enum(['no-match','no-inventory'])`.
- **Repro:** Single-building op, add a Pending point with a reachable measurement (132″) and a load high enough that `ceil(load/perStrutCapacity) > 4` (e.g. 60,000 lb; 4:1 at 132″ on LS = 11,000 lb → needs 6). The board shows the amber "No matching strut" callout though a strut fits. (The Add/Assign sheets only call `pendingReasonFor` when `recommendations.length===0`, so they correctly render the over-capacity `RecommendationCard` — the bug is board-glance-only, but it tells the crew geometry is impossible when the actual problem is escalable load.)
- **Fix:** Add a third `PendingReason` (`'over-capacity'`) to the enum, and in `pendingReasonFor`, after the stocked run fails the `!exceedsCapacity` test, return it when the results are non-empty and entirely `exceedsCapacity` before falling to `no-match`. Add matching `PENDING_REASON_TITLE`/`COPY` in `ShorePointCard.tsx` pointing at the load/engineering issue, plus a `pendingReason.test.ts` case.

**4 · Successful inline deploy expands the Pending lane and announces "Pending"** — `src/ui/operations/AddShorePointModal.tsx:303-305`
> *Deduped:* the "wrong lane" (HTML) and "assertive region announces Pending" (a11y) findings are two faces of one root cause — the inline path reuses `onAdded` instead of a deploy callback.
- **Claim:** Even when every inline deploy succeeds, `handleDeploy` calls `onAdded?.(points)` — the **add** callback. In `OperationsBoard`, `onAdded` is wired to `handleAdded`, which unconditionally `expandLane('pending')` and announces "shore point(s) added — …, Pending." on the **assertive** live region. So a fully-successful one-step Find+Deploy drops the operator on the Pending lane and (for a screen-reader user) hears the points are Pending — while the deployed struts actually sit in the In Process lane. The board's dedicated `handleDeployed` path (expands `process`, announces "In Process" politely) is bypassed.
- **Evidence:** `commitHaptic(); onAdded?.(points); onClose();` (success path uses the add callback) · `<AddShorePointModal … onAdded={handleAdded} />` with no `onDeployed` passed · `handleAdded` → `expandLane('pending')` + assertive `… added — ${where}, Pending.`
- **Repro:** Inline mode, stock available. Add a single T-Shore → Find → Deploy. The strut deploys (→ In Process) but the Pending lane expands and the board/screen-reader says "added — …, Pending." The In Process lane is not surfaced.
- **Fix:** Give `AddShorePointModal` an `onDeployed` callback (or have `handleDeploy` report `deployed=true`) wired to `handleDeployed` so a successful inline deploy expands `process` and announces "In Process" politely. Reserve `onAdded`/`handleAdded` ("Pending") for Save-as-Pending and pure-add.

**5 · Deleting one strut of a grouped multi-strut shore orphans its mates** — `src/ui/operations/DeleteShorePointModal.tsx:24-38`
- **Claim:** A Double-T (2) / 3-Post (3) writes one ShorePoint per strut sharing a `groupId`, all Pending, rendered in a `GroupedShorePoint` stack with per-member Delete buttons. `DeleteShorePointModal` commits a single `ShorePointDeleted` for one member's `spId`, and the reducer (`operation/reducer.ts:101-112`) soft-deletes only `event.spId`. There is no group-aware delete in `ui/`. Deleting one member leaves 1-2 orphaned mates still badged "groupIndex / groupTotal" (e.g. "1 / 3") and sharing the same created-order `#N` — a structurally broken physical shore. The confirm copy names the shared location and implies the whole shore is removed.
- **Evidence:** `const result = await commit({ type:'ShorePointDeleted', …, spId: shorePoint.id });` · reducer soft-delete maps only `sp.id === event.spId`. `groupLanePoints` stacks only when `mates.length >= 2`, so a lone survivor renders as a singleton still carrying its "1 / 3" Badge.
- **Repro:** Add a 3-Post → three stacked Pending cards. Delete "Post 2", confirm. Post 1 and Post 3 remain as a 2-card stack; delete two and the last shows as a lone card badged "1 / 3". The physical 3-Post is now partial with a duplicate `#N` in both the live board and the Deleted section.
- **Fix:** Make delete group-aware for pre-deploy grouped shores: when the target has a `groupId` and all live members are Pending, soft-delete the whole group in one `commitMany` batch (mirror the type-change rebuild's member collection at `AddShorePointModal.tsx:322-323`) and restore as a group. Update the confirm copy to state all N struts will be removed.

**6 · Slider commits on `pointercancel`** — `src/ui/primitives/Slider.tsx:72-95`
- **Claim:** `onPointerCancel` is wired to the same `onPointerEnd` handler as `onPointerUp`, which unconditionally commits whenever the drag crossed the 0.6 threshold — it does not distinguish a real release from a cancel. If the OS/browser fires `pointercancel` *after* the finger already dragged past the commit point (a diagonal drag re-classified as vertical scroll, palm rejection, an interrupting second touch, an edge swipe), the slider commits anyway. This contradicts the CSS contract (`primitives.css:597-599`: "A vertical pan fires pointercancel → the Slider snaps back, never commits.") — the exact ghost-commit the slide gesture exists to resist on a wet fireground. The committed action is a lifecycle status change (`ShorePointCard.tsx:309-334` → `onAdvance`/`onStepBack`). No test exercises `pointercancel` (`Slider.testkit.ts` fires only down/move/up).
- **Evidence:** `onPointerUp={onPointerEnd}` … `onPointerCancel={onPointerEnd}` (lines 94-95); `onPointerEnd` does `const committed = shouldCommit(offset, travelPx); setOffset(0); if (committed) { commitHaptic(); onCommit(); }` — no cancel discrimination.
- **Repro:** On touch, press the track, drag horizontally past ~60% of travel, then change direction to vertical (or let the OS interrupt) so the browser dispatches `pointercancel` instead of `pointerup`. `offset` is already ≥ 0.6×`travelPx`, so `onPointerEnd` fires `commitHaptic()` + `onCommit()` — the shore point advances though the user never completed a slide.
- **Fix:** Give `pointercancel` its own handler (`onPointerAbort`) that clears `drag.current`, `setDragging(false)`, `setOffset(0)` and never calls `shouldCommit`/`onCommit` — or pass an `isCancel` flag into `onPointerEnd`. Add a `Slider.testkit` cancel path + a test asserting a past-threshold drag ending in `pointercancel` does **not** call `onCommit`.

**7 · Boot failure dead-ends the field user at Splash — no retry, no recovery** — `src/app/main.tsx:22-35` + `src/app/Splash.tsx:7-22`
- **Claim:** When `bootData()` rejects, `main.tsx` sets `bootError` but never sets `booted=true` and offers no retry. `booted` stays false forever, so `<Splash error=…/>` renders permanently. There is no retry button, no reload, and no React error boundary anywhere in `src/`. `Splash` is purely presentational: on error it renders "DATA LAYER ERROR — `<raw message>`" and nothing interactive. For an offline field app, a recoverable IndexedDB hiccup becomes a permanent splash dead-end.
- **Evidence:** `bootData().then(() => setBooted(true)).catch((err) => setBootError(…)); … if (!booted) return <Splash error={bootError} />;` · `Splash`: `{error ? \`DATA LAYER ERROR — ${error}\` : 'DATA LAYER BOOTING…'}` — no `<button>`.
- **Repro:** IndexedDB.open fails or is blocked: (1) private-browsing modes that reject IDB; (2) quota exhausted so `seedIfEmpty`'s `bulkAdd` throws `QuotaExceededError`; (3) a second tab holding an older DB version blocks a `versionchange` upgrade (the open promise never resolves). `booted` stays false; the user is stuck with no way forward.
- **Fix:** After `.catch()`, pass an `onRetry` to `Splash` that re-runs `bootData()` (described as idempotent) via a "Try again" button; map known recoverable errors (Quota, blocked upgrade, private-browsing) to plain-language guidance. Register `db.on('blocked', …)`/`versionchange` to detect the stuck-upgrade case. Add a React error boundary around `<App/>` as a backstop.

**8 · Rolodex jump drops keyboard focus to `<body>`** — `src/ui/operations/GroupedShorePoint.tsx:109-116,183-211`
- **Claim:** Activating a buried member's tab calls `jumpTo(i)`, which sets a new `active` and bumps `rollKey`. The activated member becomes the front card (fresh DOM node keyed by `rollKey`) and the `<button.fs-gs-tab>` the user just pressed is removed from the DOM. There is no focus management (no `useRef`, no `.focus()`, no roving tabindex), so after re-render focus is lost to `<body>`. A keyboard/switch-control user is dumped to the top of the board mid-task.
- **Evidence:** `function jumpTo(i){ … setActive(i); setRollKey((k)=>k+1); }`; the activated tab (`i === active`) is no longer rendered (`if (i === active) return null`). `grep focus` in this file → nothing.
- **Repro:** Tab to a buried "Post 2" tab in a collapsed 3-Post stack, press Enter. Post 2 rolls to front, its tab unmounts, `document.activeElement` falls back to `<body>`. Next Tab restarts from the top.
- **Fix:** After `jumpTo`, move focus to a stable element in the newly-fronted card (front wrapper with `tabIndex={-1}` + ref, focused in a `useEffect` keyed on `active`/`rollKey`), or implement a roving-tabindex tablist. Guard `.focus()` for jsdom (the existing L-9 pattern).

**9 · Slide-to-advance has no keyboard/AT equivalent — WCAG 2.1.1 Level A** — `src/ui/primitives/Slider.tsx:85-117` · *documented exception*
- **Claim:** The lifecycle advance/step-back control commits only via pointer drag. The thumb is `aria-hidden`, `tabIndex=-1`, `disabled`; the track is a plain `<div>` with only pointer handlers — no role, no `aria-valuenow`, no `onKeyDown`, no button twin. A keyboard-only/switch/screen-reader user has **no** path to advance a shore point to Strut Set or step it back.
- **Evidence:** `<button … aria-hidden="true" tabIndex={-1} disabled>` and `<div … className="fs-slide-track" onPointerDown/Move/Up>` — no role/aria/keydown. Header comment: "The slide gesture is the ONLY commit path (ADR-026) … a deliberate accessibility exception."
- **Status / Fix:** Documented in ADR-026. **Flagged, not a silent fix.** If the exception stands, ensure each card still exposes the transition through some focusable, role-correct control for AT, OR reopen ADR-026 given the Level A failure. At minimum record the residual risk in the ledger so it is not mistaken for an oversight.

### Medium

**10 · No error boundary / router fallback — render throw white-screens the app** — `src/app/router.tsx:54`
- **Claim:** No React error boundary anywhere in the tree, and `createRouter` is called with no `defaultErrorComponent`/`defaultNotFoundComponent`. TanStack Router ^1.87 supports both. Any uncaught throw during render of a route component or the shell unmounts to the framework's bare fallback — in a production build (no Vite overlay) a blank screen with no recovery.
- **Evidence:** `export const router = createRouter({ routeTree });` — no error/not-found components; `main.tsx` wraps `<App/>` in `ThemeProvider`/`QueryClientProvider` only.
- **Fix:** Add `defaultErrorComponent` (+ `defaultNotFoundComponent`) rendering a recoverable `EmptyState` with a reload affordance, or wrap `RootLayout`'s `<Outlet/>` in an error boundary. (Pairs with finding #7.)

**11 · Seed transaction failure hard-fails boot instead of degrading** — `src/data/store/seed.ts:60-67`
- **Claim:** `seedIfEmpty` runs `db.transaction('rw', …)` with `bulkAdd` of fixture inventory. If it throws (most plausibly `QuotaExceededError` under storage pressure), the rejection propagates through `bootData` to the permanent Splash. There is no fallback to boot without seed data — yet seeding is a first-run convenience, not a hard requirement (an empty-inventory department is viable).
- **Evidence:** `db.transaction('rw', db.inventory, async () => { const count = await db.inventory.count(); if (count > 0) return false; await db.inventory.bulkAdd(buildSeedInventory()); return true; });`
- **Fix:** Catch the seed error, log it, continue boot with empty inventory, and surface a non-fatal warning. Reserve the hard-fail Splash for cases where the DB truly cannot open.

**12 · Buried rolodex members expose only "Post N" to screen readers** — `src/ui/operations/GroupedShorePoint.tsx:183-202`
- **Claim:** In the collapsed stack (the board default — `OperationsBoard.tsx` passes no `defaultExpanded`), only the active member renders a real `ShorePointCard`; every buried member renders only a tab button whose accessible content is `memberLabel` ("Post 2"). A screen-reader user navigating the stack hears "Bring Post 2 to front, button" but cannot read Post 2's status, required/cut length, or deployed strut without activating each tab (which also drops focus — #8). The group's own `aria-label` says "…showing Post 1," implying the others are present while their content is absent. (There **is** a keyboard-reachable "Show all N cards" expand button, which is why this is Medium not High — but the collapsed default still strands per-member detail.)
- **Evidence:** `members.map((member,i) => { if (i === active) return null; … <button aria-label={\`Bring ${memberLabel(member,i)} to front\`}><span className="fs-gs-tablabel">{memberLabel(member,i)}</span></button> })`; only `cardFor(activeMember, active)` renders the full card.
- **Fix:** Enrich each buried tab's accessible name with the member's status (and ideally length), e.g. `aria-label={\`${memberLabel} — ${statusLabel}; bring to front\`}`, so the rolodex is scannable by AT without fronting each card. (Keep the existing expand button.)

### Low

**13 · Same-size extensions split across rows wrongly rejected as out-of-stock** — `src/core/load/engine.ts:173-194`
- **Claim:** When a combo needs two extensions of the same size (only reachable for AcmeThread/LockStroke, e.g. `[6,6]`), the in-stock check requires a **single** inventory row with `available >= 2`. Two separate rows each with `available:1` (two physically on scene) are wrongly rejected. (Faithful v3 port — `app.js:244-258` — so pre-existing, not a v4 regression.)
- **Evidence:** `const invExts = inv.filter(i => i.type==='extension' && i.length===parseInt(size) && (…) && i.available >= qty); if (invExts.length === 0) { extAvailable = false; break; }` — per-row availability.
- **Fix:** Sum across matching rows: `inv.filter(…matching…).reduce((s,i)=>s+i.available,0) >= qty`.

**14 · Theme picker highlights "Dark" when Broadcast is active** — `src/app/routes/settings.tsx:28-31`
- **Claim:** The comment says "the 4-option picker shows none selected then," but `pickerValue` falls back to the literal `'dark'` when the preference isn't in `THEME_OPTIONS`. Segmented passes `value` straight to Radix `RadioGroup.Root`, so `value='dark'` highlights the Dark pill while the app is wearing the broadcast theme. Reachable: `/gallery` calls `setPreference('broadcast')`, which persists; opening Settings afterward misrepresents the active theme.
- **Evidence:** `const pickerValue = (THEME_OPTIONS.some((o) => o.value === preference) ? preference : 'dark') as …;`
- **Fix:** Map an out-of-list preference to an empty/undefined value so Segmented shows no pill, or render an explicit "Broadcast (via Gallery)" read-only note. If Dark is genuinely intended, fix the comment.

**15 · Lane/Deleted `<h2>` nested inside the toggle `<button>` flattens heading navigation** — `src/ui/operations/OperationsBoard.tsx:139-148,207-211`
- **Claim:** Each lane header renders `<button><h2>…</h2><Badge/><Chevron/></button>`. Several screen readers compute a button's accessible name from flattened text and do **not** expose a heading nested inside an interactive element as a navigable heading. The 7 lane titles + the Deleted title become unreliable for heading-navigation (H key / rotor) — the primary fast-scan mechanism on a long board.
- **Evidence:** `<button className="fs-lane-header" … aria-expanded={!collapsed}><h2 className="fs-lane-title">{STATUS_LABELS[status]}</h2><Badge …/><Chevron/></button>`; identical in `DeletedSection`.
- **Fix:** Invert the nesting — `<h2><button aria-expanded=…>{label}<Badge/><Chevron/></button></h2>` — keeping both a disclosure button and a navigable heading.

Notably `parseMeasurement` is *independently* dead — `MeasurementEntryModal` only **names** it in a comment, never imports it. **Per the audit brief Alex explicitly deferred the delete decision.** When the deferral closes, delete both + the coupled dead CSS (`quickfind.css:106-142`, the `.fs-meas-readout--button`/`--input` family, also zero references).

## Useless — over-engineering / redundancy

- **`src/core/load/plates.ts:53-68`** *(medium)* — `ShoreTypeDef.defaultHeader`/`defaultFooter`/`desc` are dead catalog fields; nothing reads them. The only shore-type wood auto-fill (3-Post → 6×6) is re-hardcoded as `THREE_POST_WOOD` in `AddShorePointModal.tsx:37`, which never consults the catalog — duplicating the 6×6 fact in two places (a divergence hazard). `SHORE_TYPES` is read at exactly one site, for `strutsPerShore` only. **Simplify:** drop the three fields from `ShoreTypeDef` + the rows (behavior-preserving). If shore-type-driven wood defaults are wanted, have `AddShorePointModal` read `defaultHeader`/`defaultFooter` from the catalog instead of the hardcoded constant — that is the non-dead design.
- **`src/ui/quickfind/DeductionPicker.tsx:21-28`** *(low)* — the optional `plateAvailability?: ReadonlySet<string>` prop is threaded into both `VisualGridPicker.availableIds`, but the real render site (`AddShorePointModal.tsx:481`) never passes it — only the gallery exercises it. Dead flexibility in the operations flow. **Simplify:** either wire plate-stock gating into `AddShorePointModal` (activating v3 #121 out-of-stock behavior) **or** drop the prop + pass-through. `VisualGridPicker.availableIds` stays intact.
- **`src/ui/operations/AddShorePointModal.tsx:51-57`** *(low)* — `parseDivision()` hand-rolls the same `/^-?\d{1,3}$/` + `parseInt` + `!== 0` test that `core/operation/division.ts` already encodes in three places (`divisionLabel`, `compareDivisionValues` ×2). **Simplify:** add `parseDivisionNumber(s): number | null` to `division.ts` (the module that owns division semantics) and call `parseDivisionNumber(x) ?? 1`; `divisionLabel`/`compareDivisionValues` can share it.

This is documented/test-pinned v3 behavior (`engine.test` asserts `getLoadCapacity('LongShore',40,2)===22000`). Recommend a follow-up ADR on whether sub-72″ LongShore should be unrated-flagged or excluded — **do not change silently.**

## Considered & dismissed (refuted in verification)

All of the following were investigated and dropped. The recurring reason: **unreachable in the running build** — the alleged trigger requires the deferred Firebase/`reconcile` transport (a documented no-op stub) or a caller that does not exist.

- **`engine.ts` `getLoadCapacity` `sfIndex: number` → NaN** — every caller passes a literal `0/1/2` or the constant `SP_SAFETY_FACTOR_INDEX = 2`; no path supplies a bad index. Latent type-tightening, not a bug. *(Finder itself conceded "not reachable today.")*
- **`operationStore.commit` deploy-path TOCTOU (double-decrement)** — real unserialized window, but every live deploy path is single-flight by construction (sequential `await` loop with unique spIds; `AssignEquipmentSheet`'s `inFlight` ref). Becomes reachable only when Firebase peer-sync lands. Latent store-invariant gap, not a present bug.
- **`reconcile()` peer `StrutDeployed`/`StrutReturned` skip the L-7 guard** — accurate observation, but `reconcile()` has no production caller (`firebase.ts` is `export {}`); the deploy/return events carry no `from` premise so the L-7 `isAfter` check is structurally inapplicable, and the state-based pre-flight (`status==='pending'`/`'process'`) is the correct guard. The one variant that survives the guard produces correct stock and a benign reversible move.
- **`reconcile()` deploy races local deploys through the unserialized window** — same root as the TOCTOU finding (the finder admits "identical divergence"); double-counted and unreachable while the transport is stubbed; the `StrutDeployed` staleness guard *does* exist (in `commit`, `operationStore.ts:70-73`), it's just not where the finder looked.
- **`commitMany` shares the unserialized window** — the finding's own conclusion is that `commitMany` cannot diverge log from stock (it rejects inventory events up front and its txn touches only `db.events`; duplicate `&id` aborts the whole `bulkAdd`). Not a defect.
- **`getRowSyncState()` fails open ('synced' for untracked id)** — the two-state enum is by design; a merged peer event is also "not in my queue" and is correctly `'synced'` (pinned by the passing test). The staleness life-safety guard is the L-7 merge check elsewhere, not this query. Dormant (no consumer) + correct contract.
- **Editing a legacy free-text division silently relocates it to Div 1** — `parseDivision` is lossy, but no v4 write path can produce a non-numeric division (`DivisionPicker.onChange` is `(n:number)`; `DivisionAdded` is Zod `int`-refined; no import/migration path exists). The "Roof" example is forward-tolerant display/sort code for a future importer. Latent footgun, not reproducible today.
- **`groupAdvance()` includes soft-deleted members in `affected`** — real missing filter, but soft-delete is Pending-only and the fan-out's `from` is never Pending, so a deleted member can never match the trigger's status (two independent documented invariants, not coincidence). Defense-in-depth note. *(Note: the **OperationsBoard** group-gate variant of this — finding #2 — **is** confirmed and reachable, because the gate counts `stillPending` directly. Don't conflate the two.)*
- **`lockstepCount()` shares the soft-delete omission** — same masking invariants as above; feeds only a polite announcement; the finder concedes "not reachable through the current UI." Consistency nit.
- **`getDeviceUid`'s initial `meta.get` is unguarded** — true that it's outside the try/catch (which only covers the mint race), but a rejection is caught at `main.tsx:30` and shown on Splash — not silent. The hang/blocked case requires a future schema bump (`db.ts` is `version(1)` only) and a local try/catch couldn't recover a hang anyway. *(Note: the **recovery** gap this points at is real and captured as confirmed finding #7 — but the specific "unguarded `meta.get` is a defect" framing is refuted.)*
- **Status-advance announcements never reach a screen reader (regions unmounted by modals)** — the headline is false: both live regions render unconditionally and are siblings of the modals, not unmounted by them; the finder retracts it in their own body. The residual narrow point (no de-dup/reset on identical consecutive polite announcements) is a real but minor aria-live quirk, not "announcements never reach a screen reader."
- **Buried rolodex members give SRs only "Post N" → unreadable** — the *content-stranding severity* was over-stated (a tested, keyboard-operable "Show all N cards" expand button surfaces every member at once, matching the documented a11y contract). Re-scoped and **kept as confirmed Medium #12** (enrich the tab labels) rather than dropped — the per-tab discoverability gap is genuine.

## Coverage map

**Probed thoroughly:**
- **Operations workflow** — `AddShorePointModal` (one-step + two-step deploy, edit, group rebuild), `OperationsBoard` (lanes, group gate, pending reasons, announcements, deleted section), `ShorePointCard`, `GroupedShorePoint`, `DeleteShorePointModal`, `AssignEquipmentSheet`, `StepBackConfirmModal`.
- **Core engine** — `load/engine.ts` (load tables, capacity, unrated zones, extension availability), `load/plates.ts`, `shorepoint/pendingReason.ts`, `shorepoint/reducer.ts`, `operation/reducer.ts` (`groupAdvance`, lockstep), `operation/division.ts`.
- **Data layer** — `store/operationStore.ts` + `inventoryStore.ts` (commit/commitMany/applyDeployTxn TOCTOU), `store/auth.ts`, `store/boot.ts`, `store/seed.ts`, `store/db.ts`, the `data/sync/*` seam (`syncService` L-7 guard, `getRowSyncState`, `reconcile`).
- **App shell + primitives** — `main.tsx`, `Splash.tsx`, `router.tsx`, `Slider.tsx` (commit gesture, a11y, pointercancel), `Measurement.tsx`, `tokens.css`, the picker family, theme/settings.
- **Dead-code sweep** — CSS class cross-reference (`operations.css`, `quickfind.css`), barrel exports (`primitives/index.ts`, `quickfind/index.ts`), orphaned components (keypad/parser), empty scaffolding dirs, forward-declared tokens.

**Thin spots (worth a follow-up pass):**
- **Concurrency under the real Firebase transport** — several dismissed findings (TOCTOU double-decrement, `reconcile` staleness gaps for inventory events) are *latent invariants* that go live the moment the deferred Firebase session wires `reconcile()`/a listener. They should be re-audited as part of that session, not treated as closed.
- **`MeasurementInput` typed-entry path** — the live measurement input was confirmed present but not exhaustively fuzzed for parse edge cases (ft/in boundaries, eighths rounding) the way the orphaned `parseMeasurement` was; light coverage here.
- **Phase-I stub screens** (Quick Find / Inventory / Command routes) — intentionally not deeply probed per the brief; their `ui/` dirs are empty placeholders.
